source_name: Registr smluv entry page for CNB as a publishing party (example contract record)
why_relevant: Concrete example of a central-bank contract record in the register, showing the record structure (parties, subject, value, attachments) that our parser must handle. CNB is itself an obliged publisher, which makes central-bank IT/payments procurement partly visible here.

source_name: Individual disclosed banking contract PDFs on smlouvy.gov.cz (document layer)
why_relevant: The register stores the actual signed documents. Observed examples include Komercni banka current-account agreements with municipalities and a J&T Banka legal-entity banking-services agreement. These carry pricing schedules, terms, terminal/service annexes and redaction markers ('RED' = znecitelneno) — the real evidence layer for pricing and scope benchmarking.

source_name: MPO – projekt 'Česko platí kartou' (terminal subsidy programme)
why_relevant: State-backed acceptance programme (extended to 31 Mar 2028, 60k+ devices deployed) run with acquirer partners. Partnership announcements and participating-provider lists are a direct, dated signal of terminal-estate volumes and which acquirers are winning merchant share.

source_name: MPO – Pravidla pro výběr dodavatelů (rules for supplier selection outside ZZVZ)
why_relevant: Ministry of Industry and Trade rulebook for supplier selection by non-ZZVZ entities. Matters to this cell as the legal boundary condition: it explains when a private body such as a bank IS pulled into formalised, publishable tendering — chiefly when the purchase is co-funded by EU/state subsidy. Any CZ bank running a subsidised project therefore becomes visible in the public tender record. This is the main pathway by which an otherwise invisible private-bank purchase surfaces.

source_name: Erste Group Procurement – Code of Conduct (EGP supplier rulebook PDF)
why_relevant: The named rulebook that gates EGP's standardised supplier onboarding, and therefore gates any vendor wanting to sell into Česká spořitelna. Concrete, citable onboarding precondition rather than a general CSR statement.

source_name: KBC Group Sustainability Code of Conduct for Suppliers (PDF)
why_relevant: Group-mandated qualification criteria that any CSOB-serving vendor must accept; CSOB explicitly applies sustainability as a qualitative evaluation criterion in its tender procedures, so this document is the upstream rulebook for CZ tender scoring.

source_name: KBC general terms & conditions and code of conduct for contracts (contracts_en document library)
why_relevant: Group contracting boilerplate (pricing, invoicing, purchasing documents issued by KDPB). Reveals the mechanics by which a group-level purchase order reaches a CZ-serving supplier and the standard commercial terms a competitor would face.

source_name: Komerční banka – supplier information page (private-sector buyer entry point)
why_relevant: Example of the private-sector side of this cell: a major CZ bank publishes supplier terms and codes of conduct but — as fetched — names no e-sourcing platform. Confirms that commercial-bank sourcing in CZ is largely invitation-only and not visible on the public e-tendering platforms.

source_name: Komerční banka – Všeobecné obchodní podmínky pro dodavatele (004)
why_relevant: The actual general terms a KB supplier signs up to. Gives contract mechanics — liability, subcontracting, audit rights, termination, information-security obligations — which is exactly the ground a bidder needs to price a bid and which reveals KB's risk posture toward outsourced IT/payments vendors.

source_name: MONETA Money Bank – Etický kodex dodavatele (Supplier Code of Ethics)
why_relevant: MONETA has no 'for suppliers' section; its only public supplier instrument is the Etický kodex dodavatele PDF, filed among general downloadable documents (path /documents/20143/11740692/mmb-eticky-kodex-dodavatele-cz.pdf) and mirrored in English on the MONETA ESG site. Its placement among ordinary documents rather than a supplier hub is itself the finding — MONETA's sourcing is entirely non-public and bilateral.

source_name: RBI Group Supplier Code of Conduct (Raiffeisen Bank International)
why_relevant: Explicitly applies to all suppliers delivering goods, services or licences to or on behalf of any RBI business unit and subsidiary — which includes Raiffeisenbank a.s. in the Czech Republic. Mandatory contractual annex plus audit rights over suppliers and, in some cases, subcontractors: it is the group-level gate a CZ vendor must pass. Multiple dated versions (2023, 2024, 2025) allow change tracking.

source_name: Mastercard newsroom – 'Mastercard, NCR Atleos, and ITCARD to enhance contactless experiences at ATMs' (CZ named)
why_relevant: Scheme-side release naming Czech Republic among markets with deployed contactless ATMs. Card schemes announce capability rollouts that implicitly identify which vendor/processor estates were upgraded — a back door into private deployments.

source_name: zindex methodology wiki (wiki.zindex.cz) and EconLab VZMR methodology
why_relevant: Published methodology for scoring Czech contracting authorities across openness, competition and control — including how contract-register disclosure is used as an indicator. Gives us a defensible way to weight a buyer's transparency when interpreting missing banking contracts.

source_name: ČSOB – Supplier Relations Policy / Politika vztahů s dodavateli (EN PDF)
why_relevant: ČSOB's own procurement policy document — the URL path itself contains 'procurement', indicating a dedicated procurement document tree under csob.cz/documents. Corroborating Czech-language coverage describes it as defining acceptable business practice for suppliers: conflict-of-interest elimination, anti-corruption, and mandatory acceptance of the ČSOB Group Ethical Code. This is the clearest published statement of how the largest CZ bank by assets governs vendor selection.

source_name: ČSOB Group Employee Code of Ethics (Etický kodex zaměstnanců skupiny ČSOB)
why_relevant: ČSOB's supplier policy makes acceptance of this code a condition of supplying the bank, so it is effectively part of the vendor onboarding pack. Useful for understanding gift/conflict rules that constrain how a vendor may approach ČSOB buyers.

source_name: Akirolabs customer story — RBI procurement transformation (plan-to-strategy digitalisation)
why_relevant: Vendor-published case study that discloses RBI procurement's operating model in unusual detail: a single source of truth for procurement across all 14 key markets, category strategies aligned across territories, digital stakeholder input. This is direct evidence that category decisions touching the Czech market are set centrally — exactly the mechanism this cell exists to track. Also identifies akirolabs as an incumbent procurement-tech vendor to the group.

source_name: Byznys pro společnost — ČSOB on sustainability as a supplier-selection criterion
why_relevant: Czech CSR platform interview in which ČSOB describes how sustainability entered its tender specifications (zadávací podmínky) and became a qualitative evaluation criterion in výběrová řízení — i.e. how a KBC group policy is operationalised in Czech tender scoring. Rare local-language visibility into a bank's internal procurement criteria.

source_name: CaixaBank press room — CEE payments joint venture with Global Payments and Erste Group
why_relevant: Demonstrates the third-party-parent disclosure route: a CEE-wide merchant acquiring arrangement covering the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Romania (majority to Global Payments/CaixaBank, 49% Erste, HQ in Prague) was announced by the counterparty groups, not by the Czech bank. Counterparty press rooms must be monitored alongside the bank groups' own.

source_name: CPOstrategy — RBI Procurement executive interview
why_relevant: Procurement trade press regularly interviews CEE bank CPOs, exposing strategy pillars (value-centric procurement, procurement systems/infrastructure, data, regulatory compliance and cybersecurity) and named toolchains. A reliable, low-cost channel for group-sourcing intelligence that never appears on CZ-language sites. Generalises: the same outlet family covers Erste, UniCredit and KBC procurement leaders.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf – ČSOB case study (ATM network outsourcing, DN Series cash recycling)
why_relevant: Named customer reference documenting a private-sector CZ award: entire ČSOB ATM fleet supplied, maintained and operated end-to-end by Diebold Nixdorf, ~200 DN Series recyclers, 20-year relationship, uptime/CIT metrics. This is exactly the vendor-side trace of a bank deal that never appears in any public tender register.

source_name: Dopravní podnik hl. m. Prahy (DPP) — procurement and contactless fare-payment programme pages
why_relevant: DPP is a municipally-owned sectoral transport operator and one of CZ's biggest acquiring merchants. Public reporting ties its ~1,200 in-vehicle/metro payment terminals to suppliers Bankovní informační technologie (ČSOB group) and Mikroelektronika with Mastercard, with a 6+2-year contract and revenue-share pricing — a directly comparable benchmark for payment-acceptance deals with state/municipal entities. Portal-vz.cz also lists DPP as a partner/contracting entity.

source_name: Dopravní podnik města Hradce Králové — EOC/ticketing modernisation tender pages (regional DP pattern)
why_relevant: Representative of the ~19 municipal transport undertakings (sectoral contracting entities) that each tender electronic fare collection including contactless bankcard clearing. These mid-size tenders are where payment-acceptance and clearing vendors actually compete, and they are usually announced on the operator's own site before/alongside the profile.

source_name: Enehano Solutions – Případové studie (Česká spořitelna)
why_relevant: Smaller CZ implementation partner publishing a named Česká spořitelna case study. Small vendors disclose more scope detail than large ones because each logo matters more to them — high information density per reference.

source_name: epravo.cz – 'Seznamte se, registr smluv' article series (legal commentary)
why_relevant: Practitioner legal commentary on the exemptions regime, notably the banking-secrecy exemption and its limits when a bank contracts with an obliged entity. Directly bounds how much bank-side contract detail we can expect to see and why some banking contracts are absent or heavily redacted.

source_name: GLEIF/LEI record – PRINTEC CZECH REPUBLIC, s.r.o. (LEI 315700WPP875AAWQY969)
why_relevant: LEI records give authoritative legal-entity identity and parent relationships for vendors, which is the disambiguation layer needed when the same integrator announces wins under several national entities.

source_name: GovTransparency — Czech/Hungarian/Slovak national procurement contract dataset
why_relevant: Academic research release of a cleaned CZ/HU/SK national contract-level dataset including a Corruption Risk Index and its components. Valuable as a ready-made historic panel for reconstructing long award series and testing incumbency persistence, without rebuilding the ETL from VVZ.

source_name: KB SmartPay – 'Komerční banka a Worldline rozšíří možnosti plateb kartami v ČR'
why_relevant: Joint-venture/alliance announcement between Komerční banka and Worldline covering merchant acquiring and payment terminals in CZ — a private-sector award of the largest possible kind, announced only on the vendor/JV side.

source_name: LLP CRM – case study: CRM implementation at Raiffeisenbank (CZ)
why_relevant: Named Raiffeisenbank CZ implementation reference, and it snowballs to Trask as methodology/integration-layer partner — a pointer to a second vendor on the same account.

source_name: PR Newswire – 'CSOB Partners with Diebold Nixdorf to Achieve its Vision of Tellerless Branches'
why_relevant: Wire-distributed vendor win announcement naming a Czech bank and the scope (tellerless branch transformation). Wire syndication mirrors survive even when the vendor later removes the release from its own newsroom — useful as an archival redundancy path.

entity_name: Statutární město Ostrava / Dopravní podnik Ostrava
source_name: Statutární město Ostrava / Dopravní podnik Ostrava – cashless fare announcements
why_relevant: Ostrava is a reference site for open-loop EMV in transport (VEGA CVB25 terminals across 613 vehicles). City and operator communications identify installed base and vendor generation — key for replacement-cycle forecasting and for finding the originating contracts.

source_name: TED reusers workshop materials (Publications Office) — retrieving eForms
why_relevant: Publications Office guidance aimed precisely at organisations building TED monitoring pipelines: what changed with eForms, which retrieval routes remain, known pitfalls. Short-cuts a lot of trial and error when standing up the CZ feed.

source_name: wflow.com – Česká spořitelna purchasing-automation customer page
why_relevant: A Czech procure-to-pay vendor publishing a Česká spořitelna-branded page about automating company purchasing/invoice workflow. Two uses: it evidences the P2P tooling layer around ČS, and it shows ČS acting as a channel partner pushing procurement software to its SME clients — relevant to understanding where ČS's own vendor stack sits. Vendor marketing, so treat claims as directional and verify the exact nature of the relationship before relying on it.

source_name: Y Soft case study — Česká spořitelna / Erste Group deployment
why_relevant: Illustrates the general pattern that vendor-published case studies are frequently the only public record of a CZ bank award and of whether the deployment was scoped to the Czech bank or to Erste Group as a whole. As a source-class this is one of the highest-yield indirect channels for the cell.

entity_name: Zakon c. 340/2015 Sb. o registru smluv
source_name: Zakon c. 340/2015 Sb. o registru smluv (zakonyprolidi.cz, with EN translation)
why_relevant: The statute itself, with an English rendering — needed to state precisely which entities are obliged, which contracts are exempt (incl. the banking-secrecy exemption in the bank-vs-obliged-person context), and the ineffectiveness/voidness consequence that makes this register unusually complete.

source_name: ČSOB Pojišťovna – Informační memorandum pro dodavatele (GDPR notice for suppliers)
why_relevant: Supplier-facing privacy memorandum from a ČSOB group company. Reveals-indirectly source: to explain what personal data it processes, it enumerates the artefacts of the group's procurement process — supplier records, contracts, orders, invoices, shopping-cart/purchase-order tracking. That is a free description of the ČSOB group P2P data model, obtainable nowhere else publicly. A parallel document exists for ČSOB Penzijní/PM entities.
